Title: Deep Ensemble learning and quantum machine learning approach for Alzheimer's disease detection
Author: Abebech Jenber Belay; Yelkal Mulualem Walle; Melaku Bitew Haile
Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a chronic neurodegenerative disease threatening global public health. Early diagnosis enables timely intervention. ADNI1+ADNI2 MRI images are used; deep features extracted via customized VGG16 and ResNet50 are concatenated and classified using a 5-qubit Quantum SVM for 4-class AD stage classification (CN, MCI, EMCI, AD).
Method Used: Merge ADNI1+ADNI2 MRI images; preprocess (crop, resize 128x128, filtering, augmentation); extract and concatenate deep features via VGG16 and ResNet50; encode features using 5-qubit Quantum SVM (QSVM) for 4-class classification
Result: VGGNet+ResNet+QSVM: Accuracy 99.89%, Precision 99.25%, Recall 99.23%, F1 99.13%, AUC 99.99%; VGGNet+QSVM: 95.65%; ResNet+QSVM: 91.56%; Ensemble+classical SVM baseline: 86.78%
Conclusion: Ensemble deep feature extraction combined with QSVM markedly improves 4-class AD stage classification over classical SVM and end-to-end DL baselines; suggests quantum ML can enhance classification accuracy in neurological medical imaging
Limitations: Quantum hardware/simulator details not clearly specified beyond '5-qubit'; uses Kaggle-derived ADNI subsets; resized 2D images may limit generalizability; single dataset limits external validation
Classical Baseline Quality: Good – classical SVM and end-to-end DL baselines both reported
Statistical Rigor Score: Moderate – accuracy metrics reported but no cross-validation or confidence intervals described
Advantage Claims vs. Classical: Yes – QSVM+ensemble outperforms classical SVM by >13 percentage points
Clinical Readiness Level: Low – small qubit count; hardware vs. simulator ambiguous
Notes/Tags: MRI; ADNI; 4-class staging; VGG16; ResNet50; QSVM; Alzheimer's; Scientific Reports 2024
